newsitem.title: JAPAN: M'bishi Chem likely to keep output cut into April.
newsitem.headline: M'bishi Chem likely to keep output cut into April.

text.p: Mitsubishi Chemical Corp said on Tuesday it will maintain its ethylene output rate at 10 percent below capacity through March and is likely to extend the reduced production rate into April.

"We intend to roll over the output cuts for April, although a final decision has yet to be reached," said a spokesman for Mitsubishi Chemical, which boasts Japan's largest ethylene production capacity of 1.45 million tonnes per year.
The company will decide on April production after carefully analysing market trends for naphtha prices and domestic wholesale prices for ethylene-derived petrochemical products, he said.

Mitsubishi Chemical has been restraining ethylene production by 10 percent since January in an effort to put downward pressure on the bullish regional naphtha market and to help boost domestic prices for its petrochemical products.
In Japan, naphtha is the major feedstock for the production of ethylene, which is a building block for a wide range of petrochemical products.

Another ethylene manufacturer, Idemitsu Petrochemical Co Ltd, which slashed ethylene output at its 365,000 tonne-per-year Chiba plant by 12 percent in mid-February, said it had not decided whether it will maintain the reduced production rate in April.
